title: Teaching himself clarinet and playing by ear
summary: He learned the clarinet by studying his fingers in a mirror, played professionally in five and a half months unable to read, and faked with Eddie Miller and Doc Rando.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: I didn't study under him. I bought the clarinet dick and went home one Saturday afternoon and sat in front of a big long mirror and looked at my fingers, you see. And about three days' time, well I discovered all different kinds of keys. You see, in about three days' time I could play almost any tune I wanted. And five, exactly five and a half months later I was playing professionally. Couldn't read a note. You know, keys in there didn't mean a thing, no matter what key you're playing in it. It was all the same to me. And about two or three years later I decided to go and learn how to play it, do it the right way.
Did you make up your own fingering pretty much or did you arrive at standard and fingering?

Well no, I did a lot of fake fingering, you know, which you have to do. Of course clarinet you have to finger more or less a certain way to get the tones. It's like a trumpet trumpet, you can cross fingers, cross vowels to get sounds, but clarinet you can't. You have to close all the holes to get the desired notes. Then Eddie Miller came along, he was a youngster, he was a little younger than I, and he started playing and he had a world of talent. So we started playing together and then Doc Rando, who also played with Bob Crossby, came along playing alto sax. And we had a sax team and Rando was the only one who could read. And we used to fake three way home and anything. Just played right off, just like we were reading parts.
